name: Distinct Central Square Sources Certify Relative Peeling after Attachment
statement: Let $S$ be ample, let $T$ be a vertex or edge of $S$, and attach ample pieces $P_i$ along squares $Q_i$ of $S$, with pairwise disjoint private coordinate blocks. Suppose an acyclic USO $r$ of $S$ has inward boundary at $T$. If there are pairwise distinct vertices $u_i\in Q_i\setminus T$ such that $P_i$ peels to the punctured square $Q_i\setminus\{u_i\}$ and $r(u_i)$ consists exactly of the two directions of $Q_i$, then the assembled family peels to $T$.
proof: The central orientation makes $u_i$ the source of $Q_i$. Relative USO extension lifts the orientation on $Q_i\setminus\{u_i\}$ to $P_i$ with inward boundary there, and the two source edges make the orientations agree on the whole square. Only $u_i$ can have outgoing private directions on that boundary; its central outgoing directions are exactly the square directions, so the maps are compatible. Distinct sources prevent conflicts between pieces. A directed excursion through a private block starts at its source and returns, if at all, at another square vertex; replacing it by a directed central square path would turn any global directed cycle into a directed closed walk in the acyclic central map. Thus the glued USO is acyclic, and its boundary at $T$ remains inward.
